author: Jim Granville
text: What Chip calls 'count states' here, is useful to capture a precise duty cycle. To capture DUTY coming from a small MCU with a 1% RC SysCLK, (or 0.5% resonator) you need to capture overall time and high time on the same pulse(s). The dual capture then ratio removes the remote MCU sysclk calibrate errors, and can now resolve to the jitter on the remote MCU, which is 10~100x better.

author: Jim Granville
text: These are reciprocal counter modes, and they should say 'For whole periods' as the X+ means the X setting is a minimum, and the actual capture time window is snapped to the next whole Fin cycle. Most common use is to configure TWO smart pin cells mapped onto a single physical pin, and then Frequency = (captured whole periods)/(time for those periods) = cycles per second.

dirh#msr_pins'concurrently enable smart pins

author: Jim Granville
text:
Chip's use of words time, states and periods is uncommon and thus confusing. Working from his code,  states is a gated counter, that enables when Fin=H, so a 25% duty cycle will have 25% of the value in the 'states' pin capture, that the SysCLKs captured in the 'time' pin.
Periods captures the Fin whole cycles, it can be as low as 1 for low frequencies, where nominal gate time of X+ will  auto-stretch. Thus a X=100ms min gate time, with a 1s Fin will stretch to capture a reading every second.

author: Jim Granville
text:
DOCs should state when Y updates  - I think when IN _/= ?
In a multi phase PWM design, which may have 6 or more active pins, SW would usually wait for IN _/= before doing a fast update of all pins, in order to avoid split-update effects which could violate dead-band values. All pins would be started in sync, to ensure all PWMs phase align.
Perhaps a 3 pin PWM example could be included ?
